difficultyRationale: Requires applying overload resolution rather than assuming the broadest or varargs overload wins.
prompt: Suppose a class declares `m(Object)`, `m(String)`, and `m(String...)`. Which overload is selected by the call `m("x")`?
explanation: The fixed-arity `m(String)` overload is applicable and is more specific than `m(Object)`. The varargs method is not preferred over the more specific fixed-arity match.

options.explanation: String is a subtype of Object, so the String overload is more specific for this argument.
It is the most specific applicable fixed-arity overload.
The varargs overload is not chosen when the more specific fixed-arity String overload applies.
Overload resolution can select the String overload unambiguously.

references.title: JLS 15.12.2.5 Choosing the Most Specific Method
